description: Support tiers and release baselines for the owner-selected tool roster. Tier is a maintenance priority, not a claim that a validator exists. Entries with validation_status=pending have no tool-specific validation yet. Shared Agent Skills monitoring and the second OpenCode release line are separate entries. validators lists implemented rule modules only. tracked=false entries include a primary publication URL and a manual-monitoring reason. retired_tools preserves old baselines for shipped compatibility checks but is never polled. excluded_tools receives no active support or release monitoring. Optional changes_of_interest describes validated surfaces and relevant configuration changes for issue triage.

New hook event names, hook action types (command/http/prompt/agent/mcp_tool/...), or required fields per type
Changes to skill/agent frontmatter fields or validation rules
Changes to CLAUDE.md import syntax, directives, or size limits
Plugin manifest schema changes in .claude-plugin/plugin.json

MEMORY.md load limits for subagent and auto memory, and the memory directory settings

CLI startup flags that don't touch files agnix reads

opencode.notes: OpenCode 1 line (npm opencode-ai, docs at https://opencode.ai/docs/). The repository moved from sst/opencode to anomalyco/opencode. OpenCode 2 ships from the same repository and is tracked separately as opencode-v2; release_tag_regex keeps this entry on the v1.X.Y GitHub releases even if a v2 release is ever marked latest. Validators are shared by both lines and gated by [tool_versions] opencode (rules with version_range <2.0.0 or >=2.0.0).

opencode.json / opencode.jsonc (project, .opencode/, ~/.config/opencode/ and the system managed directory)

opencode-v2.notes: OpenCode 2 line (npm @opencode/cli, docs at https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/). Stable v2.X.Y GitHub releases are filtered separately from OpenCode 1, with matching tags as a fallback. v2.2.1 publishes full GitHub release notes. The tagged v2.2.0/v2.2.1 schema review found the new timezone root key and experimental image_generate/schedules fields; timezone is recognized as V2-only and the experimental additions are already accepted. Shares validators with opencode (OpenCode 1). Review: knowledge-base/reviews/2026-10-29-antigravity-opencode-release-triage.md. Latest review: knowledge-base/reviews/2026-10-30-release-triage.md.

copilot.notes: Tracks the canonical VS Code Copilot Chat extension - the surface where new instruction-file features and schema changes typically land first. Note: the spec docs at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/customizing-copilot can change independently of extension releases; spec-drift.yml covers that path. The intermediate v0.43.{timestamp} CI tags are not flagged because the GitHub releases API returns the marked-latest stable tag.

cursor.notes: Tracked via Cursor's stable update endpoint (the same one the desktop app polls). Returns JSON like {"url":"...","name":"3.1.17"}. Channel is hardcoded to 'stable' for darwin; the version is platform-agnostic (same release ships across darwin/linux/win32). Prose changelog at https://cursor.com/changelog (readable in the HTML on 2026-10-22). Baseline 3.27.6 is the live stable marker reviewed with current official config references; the endpoint provides no per-patch release notes.

agentskills-spec.notes: The agentskills.io Skill specification (the generic cross-tool SKILL.md standard) - the source for agnix's AS-* rules. It publishes NO releases or tags, so it is tracked by the latest commit SHA touching docs/specification.mdx in the agentskills/agentskills repo (commit_repo + commit_path source). Any change opens an issue to diff the spec against the AS-* rules. Complements the weekly spec-drift.yml check. last_known_version is the short commit SHA.

muse-code.untracked_reason: Manual review of https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog and https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/configuration. No automated release extractor or tool-specific validator has been verified yet.

kimi-code.notes: Tracks the current Kimi Code CLI release line, not the retired Python kimi-cli. Release tracking is implemented; tool-specific validation remains pending. https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/

amp.notes: Tracked via the amp news RSS feed; the 'version' is the slug of the latest /news/ post (e.g., amp-free-is-ad-free). Source is not on GitHub; npm @sourcegraph/amp publishes per-commit (no semver gates) so npm version-bump tracking would be noise. Issue body uses the first <item><description> CDATA from the RSS feed (already structured HTML - no LLM needed).
